calls.prompt:
Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

[2026-22675] Notice — Treasury Department; Internal Revenue Service
Title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Requesting Comment Notice of Taxpayer Statement Regarding Refund
Action: Notice of information collection; request for comments.
Abstract: In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, the IRS is inviting comments on the information collection request outlined in this notice.

[2026-22705] Notice — Homeland Security Department
Title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Incident Communications Activity Report
Action: 60-Day notice and request for comments; extension of a previously approved collection.
Abstract: The Emergency Communications Division (ECD) within Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) submits the following Information Collection Request (ICR) to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and clearance.

[2026-22717] Rule — Justice Department; Drug Enforcement Administration
Title: Specific Listing for 3-Chloromethcathinone, A Currently Controlled Schedule I Substance
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is establishing a specific listing and DEA Controlled Substances Code Number (drug code) for 1-(3-chlorophenyl)-2-(methylamino)propan-1-one (3- chloromethcathinone; 3-CMC) in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). Although 3-chloromethcathinone is not specifically listed in schedule I of the CSA with its own unique drug code, it is a schedule I controlled substances in the United States because it is a positional isomer of 4-chloromethcathinone, which is a schedule I hallucinogen. Therefore, DEA is simply amending the schedule I hallucinogenic substances list in its regulations to separately include 3- chloromethcathinone.
